title: ORDER BY on text puts BLANK before the empty string
query: EVALUATE Texts ORDER BY Texts[T], Texts[Id]

source.supports: ASC is the default and sorts ascending; the page does not say where BLANK goes

source.quote: A comparison between BLANK and any other value returns FALSE
source.supports: BLANK and the empty string are different values, so a sort may tell them apart

derivation: Texts[T] by Id: b (1), '' (2), BLANK (3), a (4). a sorts before b. The empty string sorts before any other text. BLANK is taken as the lowest value of all, before the empty string: Ids 3, 2, 4, 1.
alternative: No source states where BLANK sorts in text. If ORDER BY treats BLANK and the empty string as equal (as = does), the tie falls to Texts[Id] and the order is Ids 2, 3, 4, 1.
notes: The empty string has the lower Id on purpose, so the two readings give different orders.
